Dated this the 18th day of January, 2023 This Crl.M.C. has been preferred to quash Annexure A1 Final Report in C.C.No.1515/2020 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Payyannur on the ground of settlement between the parties.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The petitioners are the accused Nos. 1 to 3.
The 2 nd respondent is the defacto complainant.
3. The offences alleged against the petitioners are punishable under Sections 498A and 34 of the IPC.
4. The respondent No.2 entered appearance through counsel.
An affidavit sworn in by her is also produced.

5. I have heard Sri. B. Muhammed Sheheel, the learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt. K. Reeha Khader, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and Smt. T.V. Neema, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.

6. The averments in the petition as well as the affidavit sworn in by the respondent No.2 would show that the entire dispute between the parties has been amicably settled and the de facto complainant has decided not to proceed with the criminal proceedings further.

The learned Prosecutor, on instruction, submits that the matter was enquired into through the investigating officer and a statement of the de facto complainant was also recorded wherein she reported that the matter was amicably settled.

7. The Apex Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [2012 (4) KLT 108 (SC)], Narinder Singh and Others v. State of Punjab and Others [(2014) 6 SCC 466] and in State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and Others [(2019) 5 SCC 688] has held that the High Court by invoking S.482 of Cr.P.C can quash criminal proceedings in relation to non compoundable offence where the parties have settled the matter between themselves notwithstanding the bar under S.320 of Cr.P.C. if it is Faisal.P.C vs State Of Kerala on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29416376/
2 warranted in the given facts and circumstances of the case or to ensure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of process of any Court.
8.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [2012 (4) KLT 108 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Narinder Singh and Others v. State of Punjab and Others [(2014) 6 SCC 466]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and Others [(2019) 5 SCC 688]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The dispute in the above case is purely personal in nature.
No public interest or harmony will be adversely affected by quashing the proceedings pursuant to Annexure A1.

The offences in question do not fall within the category of offences prohibited for compounding in terms of the pronouncement of the Apex Court in Gian Singh (supra), Narinder Singh (supra) and Laxmi Narayan (supra).
For the reasons stated above, I am of the view that no purpose will be served in proceeding with the matter any further.
Accordingly, the Crl.M.C. is allowed.
Annexure A1 Final Report in C.C.No.1515/2020 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Payyannur hereby stands quashed.
